title: Clean up a branch with interactive rebase

scenario.brief:
You're about to open a pull request for the CSV export, but your branch history is a mess: five commits called things like `wip`, `oops fix typo`, `more`, and `address review comments`. A reviewer shouldn't have to wade through that — a pull request should present a clean, deliberate history.

Use **interactive rebase** to rewrite those five commits into a single, well-described commit, before anyone sees them.

The branch hasn't been pushed or shared, so rewriting it is safe — that's the rule: only rewrite history that no one else has.

**Approach.** Start an interactive rebase over the five commits: `git rebase -i HEAD~5`. In the todo list, keep the first commit as `pick` and change the rest to `squash` (or `fixup`) so they fold into it. Give the combined commit a clear message, e.g. `feat(api): add CSV export`. When you finish, the branch should have exactly one commit on top of where it started, and the export code should still be there.
scenario.whyItMatters: The history you present in a pull request is part of your communication. Interactive rebase lets you turn a day of messy checkpoints into a reviewable story. It's a core skill — and a common interview topic — precisely because it shows you understand that commits are for readers, not just for saving.

objectives.title: Squash the five commits into one
objectives.description: The branch should have exactly one commit that isn't already on main.
hints: Start the rebase over the last five commits: `git rebase -i HEAD~5`.
In the editor, leave the top line as `pick` and change the other four to `squash` (fold in, keep messages) or `fixup` (fold in, drop messages).
Save and close the todo. If prompted, write one clear combined message.

objectives.title: The CSV export code survived the rewrite
hints: Squashing combines commits; it must not drop the actual code.
If `api/src/export.ts` is gone, you likely `drop`ped a line instead of `squash`ing it. `git rebase --abort` and start over.
After the rebase, `git show HEAD` should include the toCsv function.

debrief.summary: You rewrote five scrappy work-in-progress commits into one clean commit with interactive rebase, turning a messy branch into a reviewable pull request.
internals: `git rebase -i HEAD~5` detached HEAD at the commit five back and replayed the five commits one at a time according to your todo list.
`pick` replays a commit unchanged; `squash` replays it but melds its changes and message into the previous one; `fixup` is squash but discards the message.
Because the commits were replayed, every one got a new commit id — the originals are abandoned (still reachable via the reflog for a while).
The branch pointer now points at the single new commit; its tree is identical to the old branch tip, so no code was lost.

keyCommands.note: Open the todo list for the commits after <base>.
The todo verbs: keep, fold-in, fold-in-silently, re-message, remove.
Bail out and restore the branch to before the rebase.

commonMistakes: Rebasing a branch others have already pulled — never rewrite shared history.
Deleting a todo line (that drops the commit) when you meant to squash it.
Marking the first commit as `squash` — there's nothing before it to fold into.
debrief.atWork: Many teams expect a tidy, self-explanatory history on a pull request. Interactive rebase is how you get there: squash fixups, reorder, and reword before you ask for review.
debrief.interview: "How would you clean up a messy feature branch before review?" Answer: interactive rebase — pick the first commit, squash or fixup the rest, reword to a clear message, and only do it on an unshared branch.
